items.source: top_revenue_performer = the full_name of the member with the highest total won amount
items.reason: Closed-only revenue and user-performance won amounts can differ for inconsistent opportunity flags.

items.problem: The top performer fields return NULL when every ranking value is NULL rather than selecting an arbitrary member ranked last.
items.evidence_in_work: arg_max(full_name,total_revenue_won) filter(where total_revenue_won is not null)
items.source: members without a value are ranked last; ties are arbitrary
items.reason: A team with no qualifying revenue still has members, but the filter removes all name candidates.

items.problem: Team revenue and average revenue per member use closed-only revenue_data rather than user-performance total_won_amount, a source choice that needs confirmation.
items.evidence_in_work: sum(total_revenue_won) as team_total_revenue; round(avg(total_revenue_won)) as avg_revenue_per_member
items.source: team_total_revenue ... sums of revenue ... avg_revenue_per_member = per-user average revenue won
items.reason: Users without closed revenue are excluded from the average instead of contributing their defaulted user-performance amount.

items.problem: Quarterly revenue aggregates return NULL for owners without deals in that quarter, which may incorrectly propagate missingness into team growth.
items.evidence_in_work: sum(won_revenue) filter(where is_current_quarter); sum(won_revenue) filter(where is_previous_quarter)
items.source: current-quarter won revenue (sum where in current quarter), previous-quarter won revenue (sum where in previous quarter)
items.reason: A missing-quarter total and an actual zero have different consequences for growth and team reporting.

items.problem: Negative nonzero previous-quarter revenue is excluded from growth calculation although the specification only excludes zero or NULL denominators.
items.evidence_in_work: case when team_revenue_previous_quarter>0 then round(...) end
items.source: null if previous-quarter revenue is zero or null
items.reason: Staging normally nullifies negative opportunity amounts, so the mismatch is unlikely to affect this dataset.
